items.headline: Houthi damage claims on Aramco's Yanbu/Rabigh/pipeline go unconfirmed; Riyadh, Makkah, Madinah missile intercepts reported
items.summary: Houthi forces claimed Saturday strikes on Aramco's Yanbu facilities, the Rabigh refinery and the East-West Pipeline, but Saudi Arabia has not confirmed any physical damage. The Saudi-led coalition said Sunday it intercepted a ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh plus drones/missiles targeting the south, and two missiles toward Makkah/Madinah with debris falling 21km from the Grand Mosque.
items.actionable: Lack of confirmed physical damage is the key bearish swing factor for the Brent risk premium that has been inflating silver/gold-miner carry costs and EM risk sentiment -- watch for a Riyadh damage confirmation Monday as the trigger for oil (and correlated havens) to reverse direction.

items.headline: Bitcoin sinks below $80,000 in weekend liquidation cascade, recovers to ~$80,800
items.summary: Bitcoin fell to roughly $79,146 on Saturday as thin weekend liquidity amplified a leveraged long unwind, with about $810 million in 24-hour liquidations (~$689M of long positions). Price recovered to near $80,800 by Sunday but remains below its 50-day moving average, with Middle East tensions, elevated oil prices and continuing spot-ETF outflows cited as contributing risk-off drivers ahead of this week's FOMC decision.
items.actionable: Confirms broad risk-off/deleveraging across the portfolio's correlated risk assets (crypto, silver, China tech) over the weekend -- no direct portfolio holding but a useful read-through on cross-asset leverage stress into Fed week.

items.headline: Silver/gold miner ETFs post a brutal week: GDX -8.56%, SILJ -9.78%, SIL -10.23%
items.summary: Mining-equity funds underperformed the metals themselves for the week ended Friday 23 Oct, with GDX down 1.82% and SILJ down 2.11% on Friday alone. Hedge funds and CTAs sold roughly $2.2 billion in silver futures in the three weeks to Oct 13, and silver's three-month put-call skew has climbed to -3, signalling rising demand for downside protection.
items.actionable: Directly confirms the drawdown already hitting the levered silver/gold-miner sleeve of the portfolio; the rising put-skew and CTA selling suggest the unwind may not be done, arguing against adding exposure before the Fed decision clarifies the rate path.

items.headline: Gold slips to three-month low near $3,996-$4,000 into FOMC week
items.summary: Spot gold closed near $3,996/oz on Friday, down about 0.7% on the day and nearly 4% on the week -- its worst week in over four months. Markets are pricing roughly a 90% probability the Fed holds its 3.75%-4.00% range at this week's FOMC meeting, with Wall Street now leaning toward a December hike rather than a cut given oil-driven inflation pressure.
items.actionable: A hawkish Fed repricing (hold now, possible December hike) is a headwind for the gold/silver miner sleeve via higher real rates and a firmer dollar -- size any precious-metals adds around Thursday's FOMC and Core PCE prints rather than ahead of them.

items.headline: China tech selloff deepens: CSI 300 enters bear market, Alibaba and Tencent hit on Nvidia chip-supply doubts
items.summary: China's CSI 300 fell 1.8% to a 15-month low and closed over 20% below its June peak, meeting the technical bear-market threshold, while the Hang Seng Tech index hit a two-year low. Reuters reported Nvidia may fill only a fraction of the roughly $35 billion in chip orders placed by ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent, triggering a KWEB -3% move and sharp declines in Alibaba (-5 to -6%) and Tencent (-2.9%) on AI-capex-return doubts.
items.actionable: The AI-capex/chip-supply doubt is a fresh, idiosyncratic bear catalyst for the HK tech sleeve distinct from the broader macro selloff -- watch Monday's HSI open for whether Friday's +0.69% bounce holds or this Nvidia-order story drags Tencent back down.

items.headline: Saudi Aramco fully evacuates Dhahran headquarters amid Houthi attacks
items.summary: Aramco ordered a full evacuation of its Dhahran HQ on Oct 22, telling remaining essential staff to work from home, after an earlier Houthi strike started fires across several floors of the building. It is the first full HQ evacuation since the Iran war began, and the facility normally hosts the operations center overseeing Aramco's onshore/offshore fields, refineries, export terminals and pipeline network.
items.actionable: An operational hit to Aramco's own command infrastructure is a genuine (not just claimed) escalation data point supporting the oil risk premium that is squeezing gold/silver miners via higher input costs and inflation fears -- distinguish this confirmed event from the unconfirmed Yanbu/Rabigh claims when judging Monday's Brent direction.

items.headline: Iran calls US talks 'meaningless' as diplomatic track stalls; Oman shipping corridor still conditional
items.summary: Iranian President Pezeshkian said talks with Washington were meaningless even as a third tanker in two days was struck near Hormuz and Trump said he remains open to direct talks. Tehran's proposed temporary shipping corridor through Oman, agreed in principle back in August, remains conditioned on the US lifting its naval blockade and reinstating a lapsed interim truce -- i.e. no near-term reopening.
items.actionable: The stalled diplomatic track means the structural Hormuz risk premium is not going away even after a weekend price pullback -- don't treat any Monday Brent dip as resolution of the underlying conflict when sizing precious-metals and energy-linked hedges.

items.headline: FOMC decision and Core PCE/GDP this week are the key macro catalysts for rates, USD and gold
items.summary: The Fed meets Tue-Wed with the decision due Thu 29 Oct 02:00 SGT; roughly 90-94% of markets are pricing a hold at 3.75%-4.00%, with Core PCE (forecast 0.3% m/m) and Advance Q3 GDP (forecast 3.2%) due the same day. Markets are leaning toward a December hike rather than a cut given oil-driven inflation, a shift from earlier 2026 easing expectations.
items.actionable: A hawkish hold-plus-hike-bias outcome Thursday would pressure the gold/silver miner sleeve further via a stronger dollar/higher real rates, while a dovish surprise (soft PCE) would be the most likely near-term catalyst for a precious-metals bounce -- this is this week's single largest scheduled risk event for the metals book.

items.headline: Singapore bank stocks still digesting early-October bond-yield-driven correction
items.summary: DBS, OCBC and UOB fell roughly 6%, 10% and 8% respectively between Oct 6-8 as a global bond-yield surge and broader banking selloff hit the sector; shares have only partially stabilized since. OCBC separately announced a new institutional securities-financing unit and a CFO appointment at Bank of Singapore as part of a push to diversify fee income ahead of Q3 earnings.
items.actionable: The SGX bank sleeve is carrying unresolved bond-yield-correction damage into this week's FOMC/ECB/BOC rate decisions -- a hawkish global rates week could extend the pressure, while Q3 earnings (fee-income diversification efforts) are the offsetting idiosyncratic catalyst to watch.

items.headline: Singapore new-launch condo demand stays firm despite macro turmoil: Lucerne Grand 61% sold, Thomson Reserve previews draw 23,000 visitors
items.summary: City Developments sold 350 of 570 units (61.4%) at Lucerne Grand in western Singapore over its early-October launch weekend at an average of S$2,480 psf. UOL/CapitaLand Development's 1,268-unit Thomson Reserve at Upper Thomson drew over 23,000 preview visitors ahead of its official Oct 31 launch, while Q3 private home prices rose 1.4% on suburban-condo strength.
items.actionable: Resilient new-launch absorption and firm Q3 price data support the SGX developer names in the portfolio even amid global risk-off -- the Oct 31 Thomson Reserve launch is the next concrete data point to confirm demand is holding into year-end.

items.headline: Japan says it is 'months' from running out of yttrium, asks US to pressure China on export curbs
items.summary: Japanese officials warned domestic yttrium stockpiles could be exhausted within months absent new supply, and are pressing Washington to lean on Beijing over rare-earth export restrictions. Yttrium is used in magnets, lasers and specialty alloys across Japan's electronics and defense supply chains.
items.actionable: A stockpile crisis at a major ex-China consumer adds urgency to the Western rare-earth onshoring thesis underpinning the watchlist (MP, Lynas) even as those names are being swept into this week's broader metals-complex selloff.

items.headline: Goldman cuts MP Materials price target as rare-earth stocks extend month-long slide on truce fragility
items.summary: Goldman Sachs trimmed its MP Materials price target to the high-50s (from the mid-60s) while retaining a Buy rating, citing a fragile China-US rare-earth truce and a month-long sector slide; Lynas shares are down roughly 42% over six months on the same dynamic.
items.actionable: The target cut and sector-wide slide argue for patience on the rare-earth watchlist rather than chasing the dip -- China's export-pause extension (to 10 Jan 2027, per prior research) is easing the acute scarcity premium that had supported these names.
